why: The image copies the repository to /app with its .git intact, so /app is a real repository inside the container. repo_path is required on all twelve tools, so every call in this wave carries the same four-byte value and the whole corpus shares its argument envelope: with a server whose arguments are all one field, realistic overlap is total.
Bounded history. An unbounded log on a large history eats the driver's per-request budget for no extra information.
The same call with a different bound, which is what an agent does when it narrows a search. Its argument set differs from the previous one in a single byte, so nothing in it can discriminate the two.
Reads a commit body, the largest payload this server produces. If a local server egresses, a diff is the thing worth noticing it egressed.
The previous commit, so two concurrent shows differ by two bytes.
The working-tree diff with the conventional context. Read-only, like every call here: git_commit, git_add and git_checkout validate against their schemas and would act on the tree.

The index diff, whose arguments are byte-identical to the previous call's. Two concurrent calls with identical argument sets are the limiting case of ambiguity, and it is reachable with one server and one field.
A diff against an older revision with minimal context, so the wave includes one call with three fields.
Lists local branches. branch_type is required and the schema does not constrain it to an enum, so the value is the one the tool's description names.

A deliberate repeat of the first call. Two calls in one wave with identical tool and identical arguments cannot be told apart by any content method, and an agent retrying a status read is the most ordinary thing in this file. It is the floor on what content matching can do.
